To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we were able to recruit a multiracial, multiethnic, working-class sample and that our sample had a low ICC for the primary outcomes.

we were able to successfully recruit multiracial and multietchnic participants into two studies of cancer prevention in working-class populations, and the intraclass correlation coefficients were low, suggesting that the primary outcomes are likely to be measured with acceptable reliability.
we were able to successfully recruit a large sample of multiracial and multiehtnic participants from working-class populations for two group-randomization intervention studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a comprehensive, integrated, and coordinated approach to the prevention of chronic diseases in working-class populations, particularly those who are at high risk for chronic diseases, including cancer.
the development, implementation, and evaluation of interventions to promote healthful behaviors among working-class populations in small manufacturing businesses and outpatient health centers.
the development, implementation, and evaluation of interventions to prevent cancer and other chronic diseases in multiracial and ethnic populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two studies were successful and useful in recruiting multirracial and multiethnic working class participants.
the two studies were successful at recruiting multiracial/multicultural working-class participants.

the two studies were successful at recruiting a multiracial, multiethnic working-class sample, and that the estimates of the four primary outcomes are useful for planning future group-randomized intervention research in working-class populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the development of a multiracial, multicultural intervention that can be applied in different settings.

the HD studies have provided a foundation for future studies of multiracial and multicultural working-class samples and that our work has provided evidence for the feasibility of conducting group-randomized intervention trials in these settings.
the HD–SB and HD–HC studies were successful in obtaining samples that were multiracial and multiehtnic and working class.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recruitment and data collection methods used in our study are generalizable to other studies of multiracial and multiracial working-class samples.
researchers should be aware of the methodological issues involved in conducting studies in multiracial and multilingual working-class populations.

researchers should consider using a multilevel design when conducting intervention studies in multiracial and/or multiethnic populations, particularly when the intervention involves multiple settings.
